record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: Why is the formal representation of a social organization a central modeling problem for social resilience? The question asks how a demand-driven modeling process should choose a suitable representation before data collection and then decide the minimal data needed to construct it.

evidence.quote: Questions • Why is system representation a central problem for modeling?
before collecting data from an empirical system, a suitable formal system representation has to be chosen. Only then the question about the minimal set of data needed should be addressed.
Which network type is most suited to represent the organization depends on the context and the available information, i.e., data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a social organization that is to be analyzed for its resilience. A demand-driven modeling process is one in which the formal representation of the system is chosen before any empirical data are collected, after which the minimal set of data needed to instantiate that representation is determined. Formalize and answer the following:

(a) Provide a principled justification for why the choice of formal representation of a social organization (for example, as a graph, hypergraph, multilayer network, temporal network, agent-based system, or stochastic process) constitutes a central problem in modeling social resilience. In particular, explain how the choice of representation constrains the class of resilience phenomena (e.g., recovery, adaptation, robustness against perturbations) that the model can capture.

(b) Develop a general framework that, given (i) the contextual features of the organization, (ii) the resilience question to be answered, and (iii) the constraints on available empirical information, prescribes a suitable formal representation. The framework should specify the criteria (expressiveness, identifiability, parsimony, falsifiability) used to compare candidate representations.

(c) For a representation produced by the framework in (b), determine the minimal set of empirical observables (nodes, links, attributes, temporal resolution, interaction types) needed to construct the representation in a well-posed manner, and prove or argue that no strictly smaller observable set suffices.
artifact.category_tag: Modeling of social systems and resilience
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conceptual open modeling problem about how to choose a formal representation of a social organization prior to data collection and to identify the minimal data required. No general framework resolving this has been established; the literature treats it as an ongoing methodological challenge in complex-systems and network-science modeling of social resilience.
